Read a drawing back into R

Source: R/easel_read.R
easel_read.Rd

Parses a DrawingML drawing into a list of shapes that can be redrawn with [plot()]. The drawing can come from a file written by [easel_dev()], or from a workbook that contains one, including a workbook that has been saved again by a spreadsheet application. This closes the loop plot -> drawing -> workbook -> plot, without access to the original plot. The result is a redraw of the picture, not of the original plot: axes, legends and points come back as the paths and text runs they were written as.

Usage

easel_read(
  file,
  sheet = 1L,
  n = 1L,
  what = c("drawing", "comments"),
  all = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'easel_drawing'
plot(x, family = "", text_voff = 0.35, pad = 0, ...)

# S3 method for class 'easel_drawings'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'easel_drawings'
plot(x, ncol = NULL, ...)

Arguments

file

Path of an XML file written by [easel_dev()], of a drawing XML file, or of an `.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.xlsb` or `.xls` workbook, or an openxlsx2 `wbWorkbook` object. Binary workbooks (`.xlsb`, `.xls`) are converted with openxlsx2 (> 1.30) when it is installed. Without it, `.xlsb` files are read directly, but comments and slicers are not available and shapes without a size are sized from the sheet's records; `.xls` files cannot be read.

sheet

For a workbook, the sheet (name or position) holding the drawing.

n

Which drawing on the sheet to read, in the order of the drawing's anchors, or which comment, in the order of the cells.

what

`"drawing"` reads a drawing. `"comments"` reads a note or a threaded comment of a worksheet and returns it as the box a spreadsheet application shows for it.

all

If `TRUE`, reads every drawing of every sheet of a workbook (or every drawing of an XML file, or every note and threaded comment with `what = "comments"`) and returns them as one object that `plot()` draws as a grid of panels, each labeled with its sheet and position. `sheet` and `n` are ignored.

x

An `easel_drawing` object, or the list of them returned with `all = TRUE`.

family

Font family used for text. The typefaces named in the file are not used, since a graphics device rarely knows them.

text_voff

Baseline offset in em below the center of a text box. The file does not record it, so it must match the `text_voff` the drawing was written with (see [easel_dev()]).

pad

Extra margin in points around the drawing, so that thick strokes at the edge are not cut off. The default of 0 reproduces the drawing's frame exactly.

...

Ignored by the plot method of a single drawing; the plot method of several drawings passes them on to it.

ncol

Number of panels per row when plotting all drawings. The default is 3 or fewer.

Value

`easel_read()` returns an object of class `easel_drawing`, a list with the drawing `width` and `height` in points and a list of `shapes`. With `all = TRUE` it returns a named list of such objects of class `easel_drawings`. `plot()` returns `x` invisibly.

Details

Understood are most of the common preset shapes (basic shapes, polygons, stars, block arrows, flowchart symbols, callouts, `donut`, `frame`, `cube`, `can`, `heart`, `cloud`, `wave` and more; shadings and 3-D lighting are not reproduced and presets not in the list are drawn as their bounding box), shapes without a transform (sized from their anchor), theme and style colors, `custGeom` paths made of `moveTo`, `lnTo`, `cubicBezTo`, `quadBezTo` and `close`, solid, linear and radial gradient fills (R >= 4.1 for gradients, older versions use the first stop color), line properties, shape rotation and flips, nested groups, and text. Embedded PNG and JPEG pictures are drawn when the png or jpeg package is installed, including cropping, rotation and flips. Charts are drawn with the encharter package (with openxlsx2) when both are installed. Slicers of pivot tables are drawn with their items and which of them are selected; for any other object, such as a slicer of a table, the placeholder shape stored for older readers is drawn. Diagrams (SmartArt) are drawn from the shapes Office stores with them. Pictures that cannot be decoded, such as EMF or GIF, are drawn as an empty gray frame. Equations (Office Math in text) are drawn for fractions, scripts, roots, sums, integrals, brackets and accents. Arcs, underlines and strike-through are ignored.

Examples

f <- easel_dev(width = 4, height = 3)
plot(1:10, main = "round trip")
dev.off()
#> agg_record_190a42e01592 
#>                       2 

d <- easel_read(f)
plot(d)
